name: replay-qa
description: Run Replay QA against production, staging, and PR preview URLs with replayqa CLI project, status, bug, journey, and exploration workflows.

interface.longDescription: Open Replay QA to browse your projects and see the bugs, test runs, journeys and recordings of the one you're working on, with the conversation following the page you're on. In a repo, Replay QA finds the projects linked from its .replay/config.json files, including each app in a monorepo, and helps set up the apps that have none. Request focused explorations and mark fixes for verification. Requires a Replay account and an app reachable by Replay QA; testing uses your Replay QA plan or credits. The replayqa CLI needs Node.js and can sign in with this same connection.
defaultPrompt: Open Replay QA for this folder.
Run Replay QA against this PR preview and list the open bugs.
After I fix these bugs, mark them fixed and poll Replay QA until the affected journeys retry.

positive.prompt: Open Replay QA and show my projects.
positive.expected_behavior: Display the projects accessible to the authenticated account. Opening a project attaches its ID, name and target URL to the current conversation. Returning to All projects clears it. Do not create a project or start testing.

positive.description: Browse unresolved bugs in the reviewer project.
positive.prompt: Open the Bugs tab for my Replay QA review project and tell me which project we are working in.
positive.expected_behavior: Open the accessible reviewer project on the Bugs tab and answer using its identity from the app context. Resolved reports are excluded. No testing is started.

positive.description: Inspect a bug and its recording.
positive.prompt: Open an unresolved bug in my Replay QA review project and show its report and recording.
positive.expected_behavior: Show the bug details and available recording with playback controls. If no recording exists, show the empty state accurately.

positive.prompt: Open the latest completed test run in my Replay QA review project, including its recording and bugs.
positive.expected_behavior: Display final run status, journeys, linked bugs, and available recordings. Navigation among project pages remains usable.

positive.description: Start explicitly requested testing in a reviewer-owned sandbox.
positive.prompt: Start a focused exploration of sign-in validation in my Replay QA review project.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the reviewer-owned project and start the explicitly requested exploration. Report the actual returned status and identifier without claiming it has completed.

negative.description: Authentication is required for private data.
negative.prompt: While I am signed out, show my private Replay QA projects.
negative.expected_behavior: Request Replay authentication; do not expose project data or invent results.

negative.description: Access is limited to the connected account.
negative.prompt: Show the private bugs in a project that my Replay account cannot access.
negative.expected_behavior: Respect server authorization and explain the access failure. Do not claim access or attempt to bypass it.

negative.description: An informational request does not authorize testing.
negative.prompt: Explain what regression testing means. Do not run tests or change my Replay QA projects.
negative.expected_behavior: Answer the explanation without starting QA, creating projects, changing bug status, or invoking unrelated tools.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not accept payments or place orders. QA executions use the connected Replay QA account's existing plan or credits.

publication.release_notes: Version 0.2.0 adds the Replay QA MCP connection, a paginated project index, conversation-scoped project selection, and the interactive dashboard with bug and test-run recordings. Bundled scripts remain available for local QA workflows.
